chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from the one who mentioned it, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir al-Momineen (peace be upon him) used to say: O seeker of knowledge! Indeed, the (true) scholar has three signs: knowledge, forbearance, and silence; and the pretentious one has three signs: he disputes with those above him through disobedience, he oppresses those below him through domination, and he supports the oppressors.

key_terms.الصَّمْتَ: silence — knowing when not to speak; associated with wisdom in classical Islamic ethics
key_terms.الظَّلَمَةَ: the oppressors, tyrants — aligning with unjust rulers as a sign of false scholarship
key_terms.الْحِلْمَ: hilm — forbearance, self-restraint, rational composure; a cardinal virtue in Islamic ethics
key_terms.الْعَالِمِ: the true scholar — one who has genuine knowledge, contrasted with al-mutakallif
key_terms.الْمُتَكَلِّفِ: al-mutakallif — one who pretends to knowledge, the affected or pretentious pseudo-scholar
key_terms.بِالْمَعْصِيَةِ: through disobedience/sin — disputing by transgression rather than legitimate scholarly disagreement

ai.seo_question: What are the three signs of a true scholar according to Imam Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (AS), as reported through Imam al-Sadiq (AS), distinguishes the genuine scholar from the pretentious one by three signs each. The true scholar is marked by knowledge, forbearance (hilm), and silence — qualities reflecting inner mastery and self-restraint. The false claimant to scholarship rebels against legitimate authority, oppresses those weaker than himself, and aligns with tyrannical rulers. This teaching was directed broadly at seekers of knowledge in early Shia communities navigating the question of how to identify authentic religious authority amidst political turmoil.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, from the one who mentioned it, from Muawiya Bin Wahab, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘O seeker of knowledge! For the (real) scholar there are three signs – the knowledge and the forbearance (self-control) and the silence; and for the pretentious (scholar) there are three signs – He disputes with the one above him by the disobedience, and he oppresses the one below him with the domination, and he backs the unjust’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Ma‘bad from the person whom he mentioned from Mu‘awiya ibn Wahab from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“Imam Ali (a.s.), would often say, ‘O seekers of knowledge, (note that) a scholar has three signs: Knowledge, forbearance and quietness. An orator has three signs: He quarrels those higher then him through disobedience. He does injustice to those lower than him in position through domination and he becomes a supporter of the unjust.’”
